codeReview.summary: Diagnostic logging implementation for mm lifecycle tracing is well-executed. The trace points are strategically placed at key lifecycle moments in task.c, exec.c, and mmap.c. All 119 tests pass with no regressions. The implementation follows existing trace infrastructure patterns with proper event definitions, appropriate payload sizes, and correct category assignments (TRACE_CAT_MEMORY for mm events).

issues.description: task_set_mm inline function now includes trace_emit call. While this provides valuable diagnostics, it may have performance implications for hot paths where task_set_mm is frequently called. Consider adding a compile-time flag to disable trace in performance-critical builds.

trace_emit(TRACE_EVENT_TASK_CREATE, 0) at the start of task_create_ duplicates the later trace_emit_task_create call. The first simple emit could be removed to reduce noise, or the later detailed emit could be enhanced to cover all needed data.

The TRACE_EVENT_MM_RELEASE event is emitted AFTER current->mm and current->mem are set to NULL, which means the trace point shows the NULL value rather than the old_mm being released. Consider emitting the trace before the assignment to capture the actual mm being released.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The trace infrastructure (trace.h, trace_types.h, trace_events.def) provides a comprehensive event system but is not documented in .factory/library/. Workers implementing trace features had to reverse-engineer the patterns from existing code.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: trace/trace.h defines trace_event_id_t, trace_category_t, and trace_level_t enums. trace/trace_events.def uses a TRACE_EVENT macro pattern that requires understanding the format. No documentation exists explaining how to add new events or the proper event levels/categories to use.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Trace event categories include TRACE_CAT_MEMORY=0x40 which was added for mm lifecycle events. The pattern for choosing category bits (powers of 2) is consistent but not documented.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: trace/trace_types.h lines 115-122 define categories as 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80. AGENTS.md mentions debugging approach but not the category taxonomy.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker correctly followed the existing trace patterns for emit functions. Each mm lifecycle event emit function properly checks g_trace_ctx, event_enabled, and max_events limit before constructing and emitting the record.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: trace/trace.c lines 620-690 show proper implementation of trace_emit_mm_release, trace_emit_mm_release_freed, and trace_emit_task_set_mm with consistent pattern matching existing emit functions.

sharedStateObservations.observation: No services.yaml entries needed for this feature as it is compile-time diagnostic instrumentation.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: The trace system uses environment variables (ISH_TRACE_LEVEL, etc.) configured at runtime rather than services.

summary: DIAG-001 successfully implements diagnostic logging for mm lifecycle tracing. The implementation covers all required trace points: task_create_ entry/return, task_set_mm, task_run_current, mm_release/task_set_mm window in exec.c, and mm_new/mm_copy/mm_retain/mm_release in mmap.c. The code compiles cleanly and all 119 tests pass. Minor non-blocking issues include potential performance impact of trace in inline task_set_mm and ordering of trace_emit in exec.c relative to NULL assignment. No blocking issues found.
